thread:
Mike R: Heads-up — I ran a short experiment yesterday where background slab reorgs coincided with tail-heavy inference bursts and we saw 2–3x tail latency for some micro-batches. I want to propose a cooperative compacting model instead of the current preemptive reorg that just stomps on running inference.

Jia Chen: Ugh, saw that in traces too. The compactor was doing a full-sweep at 3am during a traffic spike. Do you have the flamegraphs?

Mike R: Pasted a tiny summary below, not full flamegraphs. The important bit: compaction work runs on shared worker pool and grabs large pinned pages, which forces eviction and causes extra DMA churn.

Sara L: That matches what I saw — eviction-triggered page faults spiked and GPU stalls propagated.

Mike R: My sketch for a cooperative design: allocators expose light-weight "compaction points" and a reorg coordinator issues bounded work windows. Reorg work will yield on two signals: (a) active hot inference window (inferred from kvcache hit drops / latency SLO breach) and (b) tenant-level tail-priority token.

Oscar P: How do we detect the "active hot inference window" cheaply? We can't rely on per-request tracing in the allocator.

Mike R: Two cheap signals: drop in continuous throughput (measured at runtime ingress) and sudden increase in per-token latency percentiles. We already emit per-route p99 and token-emit delays to console. Coordinator subscribes to a small set of metrics.

Jia Chen: I like bounded windows. Suggest adding a preemptable work API from allocator: compact_async(window_ms, priority_hint) -> op_id. Then coordinator can call cancel(op_id) or extend(op_id) depending on signals.

Sara L: Need to define semantics for cancel — partial compaction can leave fragmentation worse than before. We should only allow cancel at well-defined yield points that leave allocator invariants intact.

Mike R: Agreed. My proposal: allocator offers these callsites:
```
// pseudo-interface
op_id = Allocator::compact_async(max_work_ms, priority_hint)
status = Allocator::compact_query(op_id) // returns {progress_pct, safe_yield}
Allocator::compact_cancel(op_id) // only cancels if safe_yield==true
```
safe_yield means internal invariants (free lists, slab headers) are consistent and safe to stop. If cancel fails, coordinator must backoff and try again later.

Oscar P: Sounds reasonable. Two points: (1) we need to make sure the progress and safe_yield checks are cheap and lock-free-ish, (2) we should cap max_work_ms to avoid long-running kGPU mappings.

Mike R: Right. Default caps: 50ms for low-priority background, 250ms for planned maintenance windows. Also we should have an emergency fast-path where SRE can mark a tenant as "latency-critical" to abort compaction immediately.

Jia Chen: How to surface tenant-level priority? We have per-tenant traces and quotas. Maybe use routing metadata: route->serving_profile.priority = {background, interactive, critical}. Coordinator consults this when selecting which tenant's reorgs to run.

Sara L: Another tradeoff — cooperative yielding limits compaction effectiveness. If we only do tiny windows, fragmentation might never get fixed and memory bloat increases. We need decay metrics and an occasional forced long-window during low-traffic windows.

Mike R: Exactly. Plan: keep a fragmentation score per-tenant (approx using free-slab counts, extern hole estimator) and a "reorg debt" metric that accumulates when we skip work. When debt crosses threshold and global traffic in region is low, allow long reorgs.

Oscar P: Can we piggyback on existing autoscaling quiet windows? When CPU usage low and per-shard queues empty, that's a good time for deeper work.

Jia Chen: Yep. Implementation detail: compact_async should accept a reason tag so we can track why a run happened (manual, debt_flush, scheduled_maintenance). That's helpful for telemetry.

Sara L: We need to be explicit about who owns what in the interface boundary: allocator implements compact primitives and must guarantee memory invariants; coordinator implements scheduling and signal interpretation. No cross-dependencies — allocator shouldn't query global traffic metrics. Keep allocator side-effect free from routing logic.

Mike R: Good call. Also need to extend the Trace/Console to show compact op events: start, yield, cancel, finish, progress pct. infra-bot should surface long-running compactions as alerts for postmortem.

infra-bot: Deploy bot: new metric stream 'allocator.compaction.events' available on staging tomorrow at 04:00 UTC.

Oscar P: For safe_yield points, can we rework the slab iterator to be multi-pass: quick pass marks candidate slabs, next pass does relocations for marked ones. That way yield points are between passes.

Jia Chen: That helps. Also consider opportunistic coalescing during normal free path: combine adjacent frees into larger spans so compaction load reduces. Small continuous investment reduces debt.

Sara L: Perf experiments we should run:
- baseline (current preemptive reorg) under synthetic burst pattern
- cooperative with 50ms windows + debt accumulation
- cooperative + opportunistic coalescing
Collect: tail p95/p99, total bytes reclaimed per hour, compaction CPU cost, DMA churn.

Mike R: I'll prototype compact_async API in the small allocator branch. Jia, can you wire a minimal coordinator that reads p99 and queue-depth and issues cancels? Oscar, can you sketch the slab multi-pass iterator?

Jia Chen: Yep, I'll hack a PoC coordinator tied to the ingress metrics.

Oscar P: Sketching now, will drop a small patch for review by EOD.

Mike R: Thanks. If anyone else wants to be added to follow-up perf runs, ping me. Once we have data we'll decide thresholds and default caps. :thumbsup:

Sara L: +1 Can we add a short doc in /docs/runtime/ after we decide API shape? Keep it light.

Mike R: Will do. For now, logging plan and interface checklist in the PR.

Jia Chen: One more quick note — please keep backward-compat: compact_query/ cancel are optional; if allocator doesn't implement them, coordinator falls back to scheduled maintenance-only mode.

Mike R: Good call. Ok closing this thread, will open a tiny PR and assign reviewers.

Oscar P: ack

infra-bot: CI: compact-async-poC branch tests started.
